summary.text: A 27-year-old married woman with a history of dysmenorrhea presented for examination after a cystic lesion was discovered in the left adnexa; a pelvic mass had been found two years earlier. After comprehensive examinations at the authors' hospital she was referred to a specialized obstetrics and gynecology hospital for surgical intervention.

Enhanced CT showed an irregular low-density left adnexal mass of about 4.4 × 5.0 cm with indistinct boundaries with the uterus, and MRI showed a cystic-solid lesion whose solid component had restricted diffusion and significant enhancement. A right adnexal lesion was suggestive of an endometriotic cyst. Preoperative considerations were ovarian cystadenoma or uterine leiomyoma; laboratory tests and ECG showed no significant abnormalities.

Laparoscopic pelvic mass excision under general anesthesia found a faintly visible purple-blue multilocular soft mass of about 5.5 x 4.5 x 5 cm in thickened left parauterine tissue. Histology showed diffuse growth of epithelial-like cells with clear cytoplasm and no necrosis or mitotic figures; the diagnosis was consistent with a sclerosing PEComa. The right ovary showed a benign cyst with hemosiderin deposition.

At one-year follow-up the patient's laboratory tests showed no significant abnormalities and imaging did not reveal any signs of metastasis; the authors report no recurrence or metastasis. She has been undergoing regular follow-up at the authors' hospital after surgery, and the authors state that extended monitoring is essential given the potential for late metastasis.
